subject: math
title: Numbers to 10 000: Place Value, Comparing and Rounding
seo_title: Grade 4 Numbers to 10 000 Math Worksheets: Free, with Answer Key (BC Curriculum)
meta_desc: Free Grade 4 math worksheets on numbers to 10 000 for the BC curriculum: base ten blocks, the value of each digit, expanded form, comparing and ordering, number lines and rounding. 100 questions with an answer key, good FSA practice.
key_big: The place of a digit tells you its value. The 5 in 4053 is worth 50.
key_sub: Write 0 for an empty place: four thousand fifty-three is 4053, not 453 or 40 053. To round, find the two round numbers it is between and choose the closer one.
body_html:
Thousands, hundreds, tens and ones

A 4-digit number has four places: thousands, hundreds, tens and ones. 10 ones make 1 ten. 10 tens make 1 hundred. 10 hundreds make 1 thousand. 10 thousands make 10 000.

The value of a digit

The place tells you what a digit is worth.

If a place is empty, write 0 there. The 0 keeps the other digits in the right places.

Write the number

Write “four thousand fifty-three” as a number.

4 thousands, 0 hundreds, 5 tens, 3 ones. Write 4, 0, 5, 3.

Answer: 4053 (not 453 or 40 053)

Expanded form and decomposing

Expanded form shows the value of each digit: 3452 = 3000 + 400 + 50 + 2. You can also decompose a number another way. Trade 1 hundred for 10 tens.

Decompose

Decompose 3452 in two ways.

3 thousands, 4 hundreds, 5 tens and 2 ones. Or 3 thousands, 3 hundreds, 15 tens and 2 ones.

Answer: 3000 + 400 + 50 + 2 = 3000 + 300 + 150 + 2

Compare and order

First count the digits: a 5-digit number is greater than a 4-digit number. If both have 4 digits, compare the thousands, then the hundreds, then the tens, then the ones.

Compare

4503 ☐ 4530

Thousands: 4 = 4. Hundreds: 5 = 5. Tens: 0 tens < 3 tens.

Answer: 4503 < 4530

> means “is greater than”. < means “is less than”. The open side faces the greater number.

Number lines and rounding

To round, find the two round numbers the number is between. Then see which one is closer. Look at the digit just to the right of the place you round to. 0 to 4: round down. 5 to 9: round up.

Round 4362 to the nearest …Look atAnswer
tenthe ones digit, 2: round down4360
hundredthe tens digit, 6: round up4400
thousandthe hundreds digit, 3: round down4000

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Leaving out the zero (four thousand fifty-three = 453)Write 0 for the empty hundreds place: 4053
Writing an extra zero (4053 = 40 053)A number in the thousands has 4 digits
Reading the digit, not its value (the 5 in 4053 is 5)The 5 is in the tens place: 50
Writing 15 hundreds inside the number (2 thousands, 15 hundreds = 21 500)15 hundreds = 1500, so 2000 + 1500 = 3500
Comparing the first digits only (9876 > 10 000)Count the digits first: 10 000 > 9876
Rounding to the wrong place (4362 to the nearest hundred = 4360)Find the hundreds first: 4362 is between 4300 and 4400, so 4400

faq.q: What number concepts are in the BC Grade 4 math curriculum?
faq.a: Grade 4 students in BC work with number concepts to 10 000: reading and writing numbers, place value, decomposing numbers in different ways, comparing and ordering, and rounding to the nearest 10, 100 and 1000.

faq.q: How do you write 10 000 in Canada?
faq.a: BC math resources write 4-digit numbers with no space (4053) and put a space between groups of three digits from 5 digits on (10 000). Commas are not used.

faq.q: How do you teach rounding to the nearest hundred?
faq.a: Find the two hundreds the number is between, then look at the tens digit: 0 to 4 rounds down and 5 to 9 rounds up. A number line helps children see which hundred is closer.

faq.q: Is place value on the Grade 4 FSA?
faq.a: The Grade 4 Foundation Skills Assessment includes numeracy, and number sense such as place value, comparing and rounding is part of the Grade 4 BC curriculum it is based on.

sets.title: Base ten blocks: thousands, hundreds, tens and ones

A big cube is 1000, a flat is 100, a rod is 10 and a small cube is 1. 1 thousand, 4 hundreds, 0 tens and 6 ones make 1406. There are no tens, so write 0 in that place. Start with the big cubes, then the flats, rods and small cubes.

A big cube is 1000, a flat is 100, a rod is 10 and a small cube is 1. 3 thousands, 0 hundreds, 5 tens and 2 ones make 3052. There are no hundreds, so write 0 in that place. Start with the big cubes, then the flats, rods and small cubes.
Each rod is 1 ten. There are 6 rods, so there are 6 tens. The number is 2461.
Each flat is 1 hundred. There are 3 flats, so there are 3 hundreds. The number is 1308.

A big cube is 1000, a flat is 100, a rod is 10 and a small cube is 1. 4 thousands, 0 hundreds, 5 tens and 3 ones make 4053. There are no hundreds, so write 0 in that place. Start with the big cubes, then the flats, rods and small cubes.
Count each kind of block: 2 thousands, 5 hundreds, 3 tens and 6 ones. The number is 2536.

items.q: Write “four thousand fifty-three” as a number.
items.e: 4 thousands, 0 hundreds, 5 tens and 3 ones. There are no hundreds, so write 0 there: 4053. It has 4 digits, not 3 (453) or 5 (40 053).
A big cube is 1000, a flat is 100, a rod is 10 and a small cube is 1. 1 thousand, 3 hundreds, 2 tens and 7 ones make 1327. Start with the big cubes, then the flats, rods and small cubes.
Each big cube is 1 thousand. There are 2 big cubes, so there are 2 thousands. Their value is 2000, but the question asks how many. The number is 2354.

items.q: Which number has 3 thousands, 0 hundreds, 5 tens and 2 ones?
items.e: Write the digits in order: thousands 3, hundreds 0, tens 5, ones 2. That is 3052.

A big cube is 1000, a flat is 100, a rod is 10 and a small cube is 1. 3 thousands, 2 hundreds, 0 tens and 0 ones make 3200. There are no tens or ones, so write 0 in those places. Start with the big cubes, then the flats, rods and small cubes.

items.q: What number do the base ten blocks show?
items.e: A big cube is 1000, a flat is 100, a rod is 10 and a small cube is 1. 2 thousands, 0 hundreds, 0 tens and 8 ones make 2008. There are no hundreds or tens, so write 0 in those places. Start with the big cubes, then the flats, rods and small cubes.
Count each kind of block: 3 thousands, 1 hundred, 4 tens and 2 ones. The number is 3142.

items.q: Write “seven thousand eight hundred six” as a number.
items.e: 7 thousands, 8 hundreds, 0 tens and 6 ones: 7806. The 6 is ones, so it goes last. Write 0 for the empty tens place.
Each flat is 100. Count by 100s: 100, 200, 300 … 1000. 10 hundreds make 1 thousand, the same as 1 big cube.
The blocks show 2945. Add 1 flat: now there are 10 flats. Trade 10 flats for 1 big cube. That is 3 thousands, 0 hundreds, 4 tens and 5 ones: 3045.
The blocks show 1496. Add 1 rod: now there are 10 rods. Trade 10 rods for 1 flat. That is 1 thousand, 5 hundreds, 0 tens and 6 ones: 1506.

items.q: Each big cube is 1000. What number do 10 big cubes make?
items.e: Count by 1000s: 1000, 2000, 3000 … 10 000. 10 thousands make 10 000. Ten thousand has 5 digits: 1 and four zeros.

items.q: What is the value of the red digit?
items.e: The red 4 is in the thousands place, so it is worth 4 thousands = 4000. The digit is 4, but its value is 4000.

items.q: What is the value of the red digit?
items.e: The red 9 is in the tens place, so it is worth 9 tens = 90. The digit is 9, but its value is 90.

items.q: What is the value of the digit 7 in 7409?
items.e: The 7 is in the thousands place, so it is worth 7 thousands = 7000. The digit is 7, but its value is 7000.

items.q: In 5381, which digit is in the hundreds place?
items.e: 5381 has 5 thousands, 3 hundreds, 8 tens and 1 one. The hundreds digit is 3.

items.q: What is the value of the red digit?

items.q: In 8047, which digit is in the thousands place?

items.q: What is the value of the digit 7 in 2071?
items.e: The 7 is in the tens place, so it is worth 7 tens = 70. The digit is 7, but its value is 70.

items.q: What is the value of the red digit?

items.e: In 8143 the 4 is in the tens place, so it is worth 40.
1000 more changes only the thousands digit: 4 thousands → 5 thousands. 4053 + 1000 = 5053.

items.e: The 5 is in the hundreds place, so it is worth 5 hundreds = 500. The digit is 5, but its value is 500.

items.q: In 2609, which digit is in the tens place?
items.e: 2609 has 2 thousands, 6 hundreds, 0 tens and 9 ones. The tens digit is 0.

items.q: What is the value of the red digit?
items.e: The red 3 is in the hundreds place, so it is worth 3 hundreds = 300. The digit is 3, but its value is 300.

items.e: In 6950 the 6 is in the thousands place, so it is worth 6000.

items.q: What is the value of the digit 9 in 9246?
items.e: The 9 is in the thousands place, so it is worth 9 thousands = 9000. The digit is 9, but its value is 9000.
There are 0 hundreds, so trade 1 thousand for 10 hundreds: 5 thousands, 10 hundreds. Take away 1 hundred: 5 thousands, 9 hundreds, 2 tens, 5 ones = 5925.
3995 has 9 tens. 10 more makes 10 tens, which is 1 hundred. That makes 10 hundreds, which is 1 thousand. 3995 + 10 = 4005.

sets.title: Expanded form and decomposing in different ways

items.e: 4053 is 4 thousands, 0 hundreds, 5 tens and 3 ones. Write the value of each digit and skip the zeros: 4053 = 4000 + 50 + 3.
7208 is 7 thousands, 2 hundreds, 0 tens and 8 ones. Write the value of each digit and skip the zeros: 7208 = 7000 + 200 + 8.
4000 + 300 + 6 = 4306. That is 4 thousands, 3 hundreds, 0 tens and 6 ones. Write 0 for each empty place, so the number has 4 digits.
6000 + 20 + 5 = 6025. That is 6 thousands, 0 hundreds, 2 tens and 5 ones. Write 0 for each empty place, so the number has 4 digits.
3640 is 3 thousands, 6 hundreds, 4 tens and 0 ones. Write the value of each digit and skip the zeros: 3640 = 3000 + 600 + 40.
8000 + 900 + 4 = 8904. That is 8 thousands, 9 hundreds, 0 tens and 4 ones. Write 0 for each empty place, so the number has 4 digits.

items.q: 34 hundreds is the same as what number?
items.e: 1 hundred = 100, so 34 hundreds = 34 × 100 = 3400. That is 3 thousands and 4 hundreds.
9015 is 9 thousands, 0 hundreds, 1 ten and 5 ones. Write the value of each digit and skip the zeros: 9015 = 9000 + 10 + 5.
5000 + 7 = 5007. That is 5 thousands, 0 hundreds, 0 tens and 7 ones. Write 0 for each empty place, so the number has 4 digits.

items.q: 3452 = 3 thousands, 3 hundreds, ☐ tens and 2 ones. What number goes in the box?
items.e: Only 3 hundreds are used, so 1 hundred becomes 10 tens. 10 + 5 = 15 tens. Check: 3000 + 300 + 150 + 2 = 3452.
5 thousands = 50 hundreds. 50 + 2 = 52 hundreds. Check: 52 × 100 = 5200. (2 is only the hundreds digit.)
6372 is 6 thousands, 3 hundreds, 7 tens and 2 ones. Write the value of each digit and skip the zeros: 6372 = 6000 + 300 + 70 + 2.
300 + 2000 + 40 + 1 = 2341. That is 2 thousands, 3 hundreds, 4 tens and 1 one. The parts are not in order, so put each digit in its own place.

items.q: 2615 = 1 thousand, ☐ hundreds, 1 ten and 5 ones. What number goes in the box?
items.e: Only 1 thousand is used, so 1 thousand becomes 10 hundreds. 10 + 6 = 16 hundreds. Check: 1000 + 1600 + 10 + 5 = 2615.

items.q: What number is 2 thousands, 15 hundreds and 3 tens?
items.e: 15 hundreds = 1500. 2000 + 1500 + 30 = 3530. Do not write 15 inside the number.

items.q: Which is another way to make 4270?
items.e: Trade 1 thousand for 10 hundreds: 3000 + 1200 + 70 = 4270. (The others make 5270, 3370 and 4900.)

items.q: What number is 4 thousands, 12 hundreds and 6 ones?
items.e: 12 hundreds = 1200 = 1 thousand and 2 hundreds. 4000 + 1200 + 6 = 5206.
5 thousands = 50 hundreds, so 5308 has 50 + 3 = 53 hundreds and 8 ones. 5300 + 8 = 5308.

items.q: What number is 6 thousands, 3 hundreds, 14 tens and 2 ones?

items.e: All four numbers have the same number of digits. Compare from the left. 4503 and 4350 are the closest: they first differ in the hundreds place, 5 > 3. So 4503 is the greatest.
All four numbers have the same number of digits. Compare from the left. 7089 and 7098 are the closest: they first differ in the tens place, 8 < 9. So 7089 is the least.
Same thousands. Hundreds: 7504 has 5 hundreds and 7450 has 4 hundreds. So 7504 > 7450. The others are all less than 7450.
4503 and 4530 have the same thousands and hundreds. Tens: 0 tens < 3 tens, so 4503 < 4530. The others are false: 6080 < 6800, 9999 < 10 000 and 7021 > 7012.
A number between 3400 and 3500 has 3 thousands and 4 hundreds. 3462 fits. 3540 is too big, 3046 is too small and 4350 is too big.

items.q: Put 4530, 4053 and 4305 in order from least to greatest.
items.e: All have 4 thousands. Hundreds: 0 < 3 < 5. Order: 4053, 4305, 4530.
10 000 has 5 digits. All the others have 4 digits or fewer, so 10 000 is the greatest, even though 9999 starts with a 9.

items.q: Use the digits 7, 0, 4 and 9 once each. What is the greatest number you can make?
items.e: Put the biggest digit in the thousands place, then the next biggest: 9, 7, 4, 0. That is 9740.
4999 has only 4 thousands. The others have 5 thousands and more, so they are greater than 5000.
3999 has 3 thousands and 4000 has 4 thousands, so 3999 < 4000. The others are false: 5100 > 5010, 999 < 1000 and 2760 > 2706.
312 has only 3 digits. The others have 4 digits, so they are all greater. 312 is the least.

items.q: Put 9810, 10 000, 9180 and 9801 in order from greatest to least.
items.e: 10 000 has 5 digits, so it is the greatest. 9180 has the fewest hundreds. 9810 > 9801 because 1 ten > 0 tens. Order: 10 000, 9810, 9801, 9180.
A number between 8900 and 9000 has 8 thousands and 9 hundreds. 8950 fits. 9800 and 9005 are more than 9000, and 8090 is less than 8900.
All four numbers have the same number of digits. Compare from the left. 6606 and 6600 are the closest: they first differ in the ones place, 6 > 0. So 6606 is the greatest.

items.q: Use the digits 5, 0, 8 and 2 once each. What is the least 4-digit number you can make?
items.e: A 4-digit number cannot start with 0. Put the smallest other digit first: 2. Then 0, 5, 8: 2058. (0258 is just 258, which has only 3 digits.)

items.q: Put 2706, 2076, 2670 and 2607 in order from least to greatest.
items.e: All have 2 thousands. Hundreds: 0 < 6 < 7, so 2076 is the least and 2706 is the greatest. 2607 < 2670 because 0 tens < 7 tens. Order: 2076, 2607, 2670, 2706.
Same thousands. Hundreds: 6 hundreds > 0 hundreds, so 7600 > 7060. The others are false: 1450 < 1540, 8030 > 830 and 9008 < 9080.
10 000 is 10 more than 9990. 9909 and 9099 have fewer hundreds or tens, and 999 has only 3 digits.
All four numbers have the same number of digits. Compare from the left. 5324 and 5342 are the closest: they first differ in the tens place, 2 < 4. So 5324 is the least.

items.q: Put 6450, 645, 6045 and 6504 in order from greatest to least.
items.e: 645 has only 3 digits, so it is the least. The others have 6 thousands. Hundreds: 5 > 4 > 0. Order: 6504, 6450, 6045, 645.

sets.title: Number lines, rounding and word problems

items.q: What number does the arrow point to?
items.e: From 0 to 10 000 there are 10 jumps, so each mark is 1000. The arrow is 2 marks after 5000: 6000, 7000.

items.q: What number does the arrow point to?
items.e: From 3000 to 4000 there are 10 jumps, so each mark is 100. The arrow is 1 mark after 3500: 3600. (3060 counts each mark as 10.)
4362 is between 4360 and 4370. Look at the ones digit: it is 2, so round down. 4362 rounds to 4360.
4362 is between 4300 and 4400. Look at the tens digit: it is 6, so round up. 4362 rounds to 4400.

items.q: What number does the arrow point to?
items.e: From 5200 to 5300 there are 10 jumps, so each mark is 10. The arrow is 2 marks after 5250: 5260, 5270.

items.q: Round 4380 to the nearest thousand.
items.e: 4380 is before the halfway mark, 4500, so it is closer to 4000. 4380 rounds to 4000. (4400 is rounding to the nearest hundred.)
6845 is between 6000 and 7000. Look at the hundreds digit: it is 8, so round up. 6845 rounds to 7000.

items.q: What number does the arrow point to?
items.e: From 0 to 5000 there are 10 marks, so each mark is 500. The arrow is 5 marks after 5000: 5500, 6000, 6500, 7000, 7500.

items.q: Round 2650 to the nearest hundred.
items.e: 2650 is exactly halfway between 2600 and 2700. When a number is halfway, round up: 2700.
2950 is between 2900 and 3000. Look at the tens digit: it is 5, so round up. 2950 rounds to 3000. 29 hundreds + 1 hundred = 30 hundreds = 3000.
8095 is between 8090 and 8100. Look at the ones digit: it is 5, so round up. 8095 rounds to 8100. 809 tens + 1 ten = 810 tens = 8100.

items.q: Round 7340 to the nearest hundred.
items.e: 7340 is before the halfway mark, 7350, so it is closer to 7300. 7340 rounds to 7300.
9600 is between 9000 and 10 000. Look at the hundreds digit: it is 6, so round up. 9600 rounds to 10 000. 9 thousands + 1 thousand = 10 thousands = 10 000.
5555 is between 5500 and 5600. Look at the tens digit: it is 5, so round up. 5555 rounds to 5600.

items.q: The Fraser River is about 1375 km long. What is 1375 rounded to the nearest hundred?
items.e: 1375 is between 1300 and 1400. The tens digit is 7, so round up: 1400 km. (1380 is rounding to the nearest ten.)

items.q: A BC Ferries boat carried 1468 passengers on one trip. About how many is that, to the nearest hundred?
items.e: 1468 is between 1400 and 1500. The tens digit is 6, so round up: about 1500 passengers.

items.q: A school in Port Coquitlam raised $3275 in the Terry Fox Run. What is that to the nearest $1000?
items.e: 3275 is between 3000 and 4000. The hundreds digit is 2, so round down: $3000. ($3300 is rounding to the nearest hundred.)

items.q: Volunteers counted salmon in a river on Vancouver Island. They counted 6740 salmon in week 1 and 6470 salmon in week 2. Which week had more salmon?
items.e: Both numbers have 6 thousands. Hundreds: 7 hundreds > 4 hundreds, so 6740 > 6470. Week 1 had more. The numbers use the same digits, but the places are different.

items.q: By 9 a.m., 9990 people had used a SkyTrain station. Then 10 more people came. How many people is that now?
items.e: 9990 is 999 tens. 10 more is 1 more ten: 999 tens + 1 ten = 1000 tens = 10 000. The answer has 5 digits: 9990 + 10 = 10 000.

items.q: A school in Surrey bought 2 boxes of 1000 pencils, 5 packs of 10 pencils and 7 more pencils. How many pencils is that?
items.e: 2 thousands, 0 hundreds, 5 tens and 7 ones: 2000 + 50 + 7 = 2057. There are no hundreds, so write 0 in the hundreds place.
